# Helping your midwife find you
## A warm welcome from Riverside community midwives

When you’re having your baby at home, we want you to feel comfortable, supported and among friends. In the Philippines, we say the midwife is like family. That is the welcome we hope to bring into your home, too.

There is just one small thing: first, we need to find your front door.

At 3am, even a familiar street can look different. House numbers disappear into the dark, flat entrances hide round corners, and sat nav sometimes decides that your baby is being born in the local chippy.

A little planning now can help us reach you quickly, with everything we need. Whether this is your first baby or you’ve done it all before, here’s how you can help.

## When to call — and which number to use

**Riverside home birth cover starts at 37 weeks of pregnancy.** Before 37 weeks, you will need hospital maternity care if you think labour is starting. Contact your hospital maternity team straight away, using the number in your maternity notes. Don’t wait until 37 weeks to ask for help.

From 37 weeks, **phone the Riverside birth line when you think labour is starting**, following your agreed care plan. Please use the birth line rather than your midwife’s personal mobile. The birth line reaches the midwife on call, who may not be the person you usually see.

Save the birth line number in your phone and write it on the fridge checklist below. Your birth partner or support person should know where to find it, too.

When you call, tell us:

- Your name and how many weeks pregnant you are.
- What is happening, including contractions, whether your waters have broken, and any concerns.
- The full address where you are, including your postcode and flat number.
- A phone number where we can reach you.
- Any important directions, entry codes or parking information.

**Please call rather than relying on a text, WhatsApp message or Facebook post.** A message or location pin does not replace a conversation with the on-call midwife.

If you cannot get through, follow the backup contact instructions in your maternity notes or care plan. If you have not been given these, ask us before labour starts.

**Call 999 in an emergency**, including if your baby is coming now and a midwife is not with you, or someone is seriously unwell. Tell the call handler you are pregnant or giving birth, give your exact location, and follow their instructions.

## Help us find the right door

Please check that your house number or house name is easy to see from the road. A number hidden behind a plant is lovely for the plant, but not much use to a midwife.

If your home has a name rather than a number, tell us exactly where it is. For example:

> “Rosemary Cottage is the blue door between numbers 22 and 26. The name is on the gate.”

Useful directions include a nearby junction, a clear landmark, the colour of your door, or which side of the road you are on. Tell us if sat nav regularly sends visitors to the wrong place.

**At night, please put the porch or outside light on, if you have one.** A light in a front window can help, too.

A bright ribbon or another clear marker on the gate may make your home easier to spot. One family used balloons, which certainly helped us find the party! Just tell us what we are looking for, and keep the entrance clear.

## Flats: tell us the whole journey

A flat number does not always tell the whole story. Flat 14 may be in a different building from flat 13. We have learned this the long way round.

Please tell us:

- The name or number of your building or block.
- Which entrance to use, especially if there is more than one.
- Your floor and flat number.
- How the buzzer or entry system works.
- Whether there is a lift, and whether it is working.
- Any gates, locked doors or steps on the way in.

If someone can safely meet us at the entrance, that can help. **Nobody needs to leave you alone or miss the birth to stand outside**, though. Clear directions and a working buzzer are much better than a worried partner waving a tea towel from an upstairs window.

For your privacy, share door codes and exact location details directly with the team, not in the Facebook group.

## A location pin can help

A map pin or a what3words location can be useful, particularly when an entrance is hard to find.

Check that the location points to **the entrance we should use**, rather than the middle of your building, a back garden or the next street.

Ask us in advance whether the Riverside birth line phone can receive WhatsApp messages or location pins, and how to send them. Don’t assume that a message has arrived or been read. Always give your full address during the phone call as well.

## Two midwives, two cars — and quite a lot of kit

Two midwives usually come for the birth, often in separate cars. If possible, please plan for **two nearby parking spaces**.

We bring equipment such as gas and air cylinders and large bags, and sometimes pool equipment. A short, clear route from the car to your door makes a real difference. Our arms will thank you.

If your street has permit parking, including in parts of Anfield and Kensington, check the current rules with the council before your due date. Ask about visitor permits and how they must be used. Some permits need to be activated electronically; others must be displayed correctly.

If a paper permit is needed, have it ready for us to put in the vehicle. A permit on your own dashboard will not necessarily cover ours.

Please don’t block pavements, neighbours’ access or emergency routes. If parking is difficult, tell us in advance. We can plan together.

## Give us a clear path

You do not need a spotless house. You are preparing to have a baby, not entering a cleaning competition.

What helps is a clear route from the front door to the room you plan to use, and to the toilet. Please move shoes, washing baskets, loose cables and other trip hazards out of the way.

Check the stairs, too. Lego is impressive engineering, but none of us wants to test it with our feet while carrying a cylinder.

Agree who will let us in. There is no need to leave your front door open or unlocked while you wait. We would much rather knock than accidentally meet your neighbour over a Jammie Dodger.

## We love your pets. We also need both feet on the floor.

Even a friendly pet can become excited or worried when new people and equipment arrive.

Please arrange for pets to stay safely in another room or with someone who can look after them. This helps us carry equipment in and keeps the space around you clear.

If you have an assistance dog, let us know beforehand so we can plan with you.

## No perfect house required

These are practical ways to help, not a test you have to pass. You do not need a driveway, a porch light or someone available to wait outside.

If anything here is difficult, tell us at a visit. We will work out a plan together. Our job is to care for you and your baby, not judge your home.

We are looking forward to meeting your newest family member. Help us find the door, and we will take it from there.

---

## Fridge checklist: ready for Riverside

**My full address and postcode:**  
__________________________________________________

**Riverside birth line:**  
__________________________________________________

**Backup maternity contact, as agreed with the team:**  
__________________________________________________

☐ I know home birth cover starts at **37 weeks**.

☐ I know to **phone the birth line when labour starts**, not a personal mobile.

☐ My birth partner or support person knows the calling plan.

☐ My house number or name is easy to see.

☐ I have shared any tricky directions, flat entrances and entry arrangements.

☐ I know how to share a location pin, if the team accepts one.

☐ I have checked parking and any visitor permit arrangements.

☐ I have planned space for two cars, where possible.

☐ Outside lighting is on at night, if available.

☐ Hallways, stairs and the route into the birth room are clear.

☐ There is a safe plan for pets.

☐ We know who will answer the door.

**Emergency: call 999. Do not delay an emergency call while completing this checklist.**
